## Audit E09: recursive delegation, M round 3

**Outcome.** The student stopped to request clarification rather than implementing the task. The submitted patch was empty, and the formal verifier graded the pristine base: 0/7 fail-to-pass tests and 31/31 pass-to-pass tests, binary reward 0. This is an **empty-patch outcome**, not evidence that an attempted delegation algorithm failed. The verifier ran successfully; its exit code 0 is not a passing grade. Sources: `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/hint-codex-experiments/runs/codex_parallel_12/lanes/codex_parallel_12_lane0/codex_parallel_12_lane0_M_r3/infer_logs/claude-code-by-agents-recursive-delegation/turn_1/patch.diff` and `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/hint-codex-experiments/runs/codex_parallel_12/lanes/codex_parallel_12_lane0/codex_parallel_12_lane0_M_r3/eval_output/claude-code-by-agents-recursive-delegation/eval_result.json`.

**Actual work and stop.** The requested work was recursive `delegate_task` execution and parent continuation, including matching tool IDs and distinct unknown-agent, child-error, empty-output and circular-delegation behavior, on a new branch with a commit. In `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/hint-codex-experiments/runs/codex_parallel_12/lanes/codex_parallel_12_lane0/codex_parallel_12_lane0_M_r3/infer_logs/claude-code-by-agents-recursive-delegation/turn_1/trajs.json`, main_agent events 1–3 show invocation and delivery of the `claude-api` skill. Its visible instructions said to stop and ask about non-Anthropic provider markers. Events 4–5 show an independent repository listing, Git status/branch inspection and provider-marker search; the output included `backend/providers/openai.ts` and a detached HEAD. Event 6 asked whether the implementation should be provider-neutral or Anthropic-only and stated that no branch, changes, tests or commit had been made. The recorded stop reason was `end_turn`, not a recorded tool or API failure. The skill instruction and observed search explain the immediate stop; the record does not establish why the skill was invoked.

There was no local implementation or test run to compare with the formal check. The formal seven failures cover circularity, child errors, execution, empty text, unknown agents, empty instructions and multilevel delegation. The 31 passing existing tests and partial score of 0.815789 do not constitute task success, and even a finite passing official grade would not by itself prove the entire public contract.

**Knowledge received versus adoption.** The captured initial prompt, `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/hint-codex-experiments/runs/codex_parallel_12/lanes/codex_parallel_12_lane0/codex_parallel_12_lane0_M_r3/infer_logs/claude-code-by-agents-recursive-delegation/turn_1/system_prompt_actual.json`, actually contained a problem-solving reference. It described a recursive provider-tool round trip, handler-owned execution, adapter translation, request-specific availability, matching IDs, recursion safety and several source-location clues. It also demanded independent verification and prohibited attribution to the reference. Those instructions make first-person self-claims alone weak evidence of independent discovery; here, however, the visible student did not even claim to implement the approach. The provider-marker search was observable independent exploration, but it did not establish source-level verification or executable adoption of the reference. The reference’s conditional discussion of read-only work did not itself establish that this student was prohibited from writing.

Archived Hint files being available would not alone show receipt; the captured prompt does show receipt here. After-round reviews are not this round’s inputs. Individual event strings were clipped at 1,800 characters in the supplied evidence, so unseen portions cannot support stronger claims; the captured initial prompt, final patch and formal evaluation were supplied separately without that event-field clipping.

**Conditions and comparison limits.** The recorded session used `gpt-6.1-terra`, Claude Code 2.1.329 via the SDK, `bypassPermissions`, and no MCP servers. It reported three model calls, 154,860 input and 272 output tokens; the ledger inventory records 14,592 cached input tokens, while session usage reports zero cache-read tokens. The SDK’s $0.7811 estimate has unknown cost basis and is not established actual CLI billing. Historical costs not supplied are unknown, not zero.

The supplied evidence contains only this historical round, not a no-Hint full pass, I2’s underlying record, or prior patches. Therefore it cannot establish that a teacher is necessary, that I2 was the sole success, or that this empty patch regressed from an earlier implementation. Model, runtime, budget and tool-setting equivalence to batch 12/source 13 is not established, so no causal group comparison is warranted. A possible lesson to investigate is whether scope-gating by a provider-specific skill can interrupt otherwise actionable work; this is a hypothesis, not measured transfer or a ranked learning-value finding.
